# Pandamonium v1.0.57

This release collects everything on main since v1.0.55: real, bound chat projects; the Settings protocol-panel and raw JSON editor removal; tailnet model discovery; the docked-modal renderer freeze fix; and the queued-message strip that now docks above the composer with Steer, Edit, and Delete.

## MAD-920 — Projects: make chat projects real, bound, and part of Chats

### Problem

Projects appeared twice: a standalone sidebar Projects section and a "Projects" group inside Chats that was actually free-form `session.folder` strings, unbound to anything. Chats could be grouped under names that did not correspond to real directories.

### Implementation

Sessions now carry `sessions.project_id` (additive column + migration); session create/PATCH accept it; removing a project unbinds its chats. New project folders are stamped from the WhoAmI project-local-ai-growth starter (AGENTS.md, HANDOVER.md, MEMORY.md, BUGS.md, STATUS.md, SYSTEM-MAP.md, DECISIONS.md, BACKLOG.md, IMPORT.md, tickets/, evidence/, artifacts/) with existing files never overwritten and imported folders untouched. A one-time idempotent startup migration converts legacy chat folder names into projects and binds their chats (excluding Tasks and Assistant), and auto-sort assigns chats to existing projects only.

### Product value and UI visibility

The standalone Projects section is gone; a Projects group inside Chats lists real projects with create/import (+), session counts, a hover + to start a session bound to that project, and a hover × to unregister it (folder and chats stay). Selecting a project-bound chat sets the project workspace.

### Verification

Full Python suite: 5,772 passed / 5 skipped. Full browser suite: 109 passed. New `tests/test_projects_in_chats.py` covers scaffold/no-overwrite/import, migration exclusions and idempotency, unbind-on-remove, route validation, PATCH binding/clearing, list projection, and frontend source guards.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Additive schema; existing chats and folders keep working. Project move handles are invisible at rest and appear on row hover, focus-within, or rearrange mode. Ships from the parallel workspace lane (PR #153).

## MAD-928 — Settings: remove the Protocols panel and raw model-window/budget editors

### Problem

Settings → AI Defaults exposed protocols as operator checkboxes ("Mount the protocol layer", JOS-IPAV, JOS-P0–P7) plus two raw JSON editors for model context windows and input token budgets. Protocols are how the agent works inside Pandamonium and mount by design, not an operator switch, and the JSON editors were unusable in practice.

### Implementation

Removed the Protocols card and its front-end wiring: `initProtocolSettings()` and its call are gone, and `static/js/settings.js` no longer reads or posts `protocol_layer_enabled`, `disabled_protocol_packs`, `model_context_windows`, or `model_input_token_budgets`. Runtime protocol mounting, the diagnostics route, and discovery-driven windows/budgets are unchanged.

### Product value and UI visibility

Settings → AI Defaults now shows Agent Identity and the model-default sections only; the protocol panel, pack checkboxes, and both JSON editors are gone. No replacement editor is added.

### Verification

New `tests/test_protocol_settings_removed.py` source guard plus all five runtime protocol suites passed (31 tests). New `tests/browser/protocol-settings-removed.spec.js` asserts the panel and JSON editors are absent, no `/api/diagnostics/protocol/packs` request fires from Settings, and the identity/model-default cards still render. `node --check static/js/settings.js` is clean.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

UI-only removal. Existing saved settings keys remain in the settings store but are no longer edited from the UI, and runtime behavior is unchanged. Model context windows and input budgets continue to resolve from the discovered provider catalog (MAD-897/903).

## MAD-933 — Models: add tailnet scan and "Add Tailscale Models" to Add Models

### Problem

"Scan Models" only probed local ports; the bounded tailnet discovery API existed but the Settings UI never called it, and there was no operator-facing way to register a model server running on another tailnet node. Worker/agent connectivity was hardcoded, so a normal user could not connect their own nodes.

### Implementation

Added an "Add Tailscale Models" card to Settings → Add Models. Scan Tailnet lists online peers through the existing bounded discovery API (opaque peer ids and OS only, 120s TTL, up to 5 selected); the operator selects peers, probes them, and each finding registers through `POST /api/model-endpoints` with `endpoint_kind=tailnet`. The browser never receives peer addresses: the new `resolve_tailnet_candidate` resolves the address server-side from the issued peer selection and returns the base URL only to the registration path. Ollama candidates register at the root URL; OpenAI-compatible candidates at `/v1`. Manual tailnet URL entry is the fallback, and Added Models now groups endpoints into Local / API / Tailnet. Tailnet endpoints use local-class refresh intervals and timeouts.

### Product value and UI visibility

Any tailnet node running a model server can be connected from Settings without an agent's help. Tailnet endpoints appear under Added Models → Tailnet with their model counts, and their models show up in the composer picker like any other endpoint.

### Verification

`tests/test_safe_tailnet_discovery.py` covers probe-free/redacted peer listing, probe candidates exposing port but not address, server-side base URL resolution for OpenAI-compatible and Ollama targets, and TTL/unknown-port rejection. `tests/test_model_routes.py` covers tailnet kind classification, server-side resolution during create, and 400s for incomplete or unissued selections. `tests/browser/tailnet-models.spec.js` drives scan → select → probe → per-row add and the manual URL path. Focused Python set: 240 passed; browser: 2 passed.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Additive: `tailnet` is a new endpoint kind and existing endpoints keep their Local/API grouping. Peer addresses stay server-side and are not returned by discovery responses. The 5-peer selection limit, peer-id TTL, and bounded probe behavior are reused unchanged. Agent endpoints and SSH connections remain future M16 slices.

### References

## MAD-942 — UI: stop the modal z-stack observer from freezing the renderer

### Problem

When a side-docked tool (for example the Pandamonium Updater) was already open, clicking Settings, the profile button, or another sidebar tool froze the renderer until Chrome killed the tab.

### Implementation

The global modal z-stack observer in `static/js/ui.js` promoted every class and style mutation on a visible `.modal`. Because `_promote` writes an inline z-index, that write re-fired the same observer; with two visible modals each batch raised one above the other forever in a microtask loop (`_zCounter` climbed 1000 → 2028). Promotion now happens on visibility transitions only: each modal's last visible state is tracked in a `WeakMap`, and cosmetic writes on an already-visible modal no longer trigger promotion. "Most recently opened wins" is preserved.

### Product value and UI visibility

Settings, the profile menu, and sidebar tools open normally while another docked tool is visible; the renderer no longer locks up.

### Verification

New `tests/browser/mad-942-dock-freeze.spec.js`: 3 passed, and the same tests fail with the pre-fix `ui.js`. Existing `modal-lifecycle.spec.js` plus `mad-899-ui-batch.spec.js`: 31 passed.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend z-order logic only; no API, schema, or data change. Ships from the parallel workspace lane (PR #163).

### References

- [Linear MAD-942](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-942/ui-stop-modal-z-stack-observer-from-freezing-the-renderer)

## MAD-943 — Chat: dock queued messages above the composer with Steer and Edit/Delete

### Problem

While the agent was streaming, a submitted follow-up was queued correctly but rendered as a full user chat bubble at the end of `#chat-history` with a "Queued" pill. The bubble looked like an already-sent message, cluttered the transcript, and offered no per-item controls; the click-to-send-now behavior was undiscoverable.

### Implementation

Queued messages now render in a compact strip (`#chat-queue-strip`) docked inside `.chat-input-bar` directly above the composer instead of the chat history. Each card carries a queue icon, the truncated message text, a **Steer** button, and a **...** menu with inline **Edit** (Enter saves, Escape cancels, Save disabled when empty) and **Delete**. Steer reuses the existing promote path: it stops the active response and sends that item immediately; multi-item queues stay FIFO and the existing stream-end drain removes each card as it sends. The old `.msg-user-queued` bubble markup and styles, the queue toast, and the queue bubble host were removed.

### Product value and UI visibility

Queued follow-ups appear exactly where the next message is typed, matching the expected queue surface: text truncates to one line, Steer sends immediately, and Edit/Delete are one click away. The transcript stays clean and queued text is never mistaken for a sent message.

### Verification

New `tests/browser/chat-queue.spec.js` (4 passed): dock placement above the composer with no chat-history bubble, inline edit + delete with order preserved, Steer stopping the active response and sending immediately, and FIFO drain on stream completion. Adjacent regressions `new-chat.spec.js`, `chat-composer-mermaid.spec.js`, and `mad-899-ui-batch.spec.js` passed 15/15; `node --check` and `git diff --check` are clean; PR CI passed all checks.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend-only: no backend, schema, dependency, or data changes. Enter/Send/mobile submit entry points and stream-end auto-send are unchanged. True mid-turn steering/injection into the running model turn and queue persistence across page reload are out of scope.

### References

## MAD-922 — Onboarding: guided setup wizard with live setup status

### Problem

A new admin met a passive setup checklist that deep-linked into dense Settings panels (`#welcome-setup`), while non-admins saw a "type /setup" invite that could only 403. There was no live view of what was actually configured and no single first-run path for naming the assistant and reaching a usable model.

### Implementation

Added a wizard host modal and `static/js/setupWizard.js` with a step framework (progress, Back, Skip, Next/resume) that replaces the passive checklist. A new read-only `GET /api/setup/status` derives live booleans from existing owners (identity configured, model usable, voice ready, portal connected, plugin count, gallery connected, update state, `is_admin`) with admin-only fields gated and the agent constitution never included. The admin wizard auto-opens while required steps (identity, model) are incomplete, dismissal persists across tabs, and the Guide button reopens the status home with live checkmarks. The identity step saves the display name through the existing `POST /api/auth/settings`; non-admins get a status-only "Managed by your administrator" view and lose the 403-prone invite.

### Product value and UI visibility

A fresh install now walks the admin through naming the assistant and connecting a model, then shows a live status home. The Guide button reopens it at any time, and non-admin users see done/managed rows instead of controls they cannot use.

### Verification

`tests/test_setup_status.py`, `tests/test_setup_wizard_ui.py`, `tests/test_identity_first_run.py`, and `tests/test_personal_books.py` passed 33 focused tests; `tests/browser/setup-wizard.spec.js` plus `ui-polish.spec.js` passed 5; the full tracked browser suite passed 76; `python -c 'import app'` reported the new route (81 → 82).

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Additive: no new dependencies, no schema changes, no admin route changes. Existing guide-modal behavior is preserved and dismissal is persistent. Live CT103 acceptance remains tracked separately on MAD-922.
